thread:
sofia-peopleops: Hi team — new hire Raj P. (candidate) lost his original I-797 approval notice while documents were in transit to the consulate. Recruiter uploaded a scanned I-797 but the consulate is requesting the original for the visa appointment. Can people-ops confirm the safest/fastest path to request a duplicate approval notice from USCIS and whether Redwood covers courier or counsel fees? cc @mike-recruiter

mike-recruiter: Candidate is in Bangalore, visa appointment booked for Apr 12. He has passport + I-94 copy, just missing the original I-797. He can wait a bit but worried consulate will deny without original.

anya-legal: Short answer: we'll engage external counsel to request a duplicate approval and/or consulate notification. I'll contact our immigration attorney now for the exact mechanism and timeline (some cases use a formal replacement request, others get a consulate notification or certified copy). I'll ask counsel if they can prioritize and whether premium options exist.

people-ops-bot: Reminder: expense workflow for immigration costs => use /expense create, Category: "Immigration/Relocation", attach counsel quote and courier estimate.

sofia-peopleops: Thanks @anya-legal. To be clear: please confirm expected turnaround and an estimate so we can approve expenses. @mike-recruiter please tell Raj not to send his passport to anyone yet until we confirm the safest shipping method.

mike-recruiter: Told Raj to hold on passport shipments. He said local USCIS office has a 4–6 week wait for appointments. Not ideal for Apr 12 schedule.

anya-legal: Counsel (Fragomen) responded — they can submit a consulate notification or seek a duplicate approval depending on the service center. They asked for scanned passport, scanned I-797, and signed POA from the candidate. Fragomen said expedited handling is possible for an additional fee; they will provide a fee estimate in 24 hours.

sofia-peopleops: Ok I'm pre-approving up to $800 for courier + local handling while we wait for counsel's formal quote. If counsel requests premium processing >$2500, we'll escalate to head approval.

lina-head-peopleops: Approved emergency cap increased to $2500 this quarter for emergent visa cases. Please tag hiring cost center when submitting expenses.

mike-recruiter: Candidate consents to share scans and sign POA. I'll upload the signed POA and scanned docs to the Fragomen intake link once I get them. I'll also add a short candidate consent note to the ticket.

anya-legal: Filed intake with counsel; Fragomen created case FRG-2026-877. They requested the offer letter and HR contact. I'll DM the candidate the POA template for e-sign. Will update here when they confirm next steps.

sofia-peopleops: Great — please keep this thread live. If consulate insists on original, plan is to ship via FedEx Priority with signature required and notify candidate of tracking. Also keep receipts for reimbursement. :thumbsup:

mike-recruiter: Will do. Posting consent and scans in 10–15m.

anya-legal: Update: Fragomen estimates 48–72 hours for urgent consulate notification and ~$600–$900 for handling + courier. If Radial premium filing is required it could be higher; will confirm exact amount.

sofia-peopleops: Thanks all. I'll submit a tentative expense request so we have a PO ready. Keep updates short in this thread.

lina-head-peopleops: Thanks team — appreciate quick turnaround.
